The post-application waiting period
stories.summary: Students who submitted Early Decision or Early Action applications are advised that the period before mid-December admissions results is not for relaxing. With Regular Decision deadlines arriving in early January, the college application process remains active. Senior year is apparently not yet over.

stories.title: AI is Transforming Business Careers: Which Roles are Rising and Falling, and How Altera Institute Prepares its Students
Visualizing manufacturing for students
stories.summary: Educators are using Meshy AI to generate 3D models of machinery to explain manufacturing roles to Racine County students. Because the software may produce inaccurate technical details, the school suggests that someone with actual manufacturing experience review the generated assets before they reach the classroom.

stories.title: Employee engagement hits 15-year low
stories.summary: Gallup reports that American employee engagement fell to 29 percent in the third quarter of 2026, the lowest level since 2011. While workplaces anticipated that AI would handle repetitive tasks and improve work-life balance, the tools have left many employees feeling disconnected from their jobs.

stories.title: Students study the work of democracy
stories.summary: A University of Wisconsin-Madison student helped organize a local session where residents debated housing policy. After observing the complexity of public consensus, including conflicting priorities like transportation and park access, the student changed his major from political science. Democracy is reportedly more complicated than the data suggests.

stories.title: 5 Best SAT Prep Courses: Which One Is for You? - Charlotte Observer
Gemini adds SAT practice exams
stories.summary: Gemini now offers full-length SAT practice exams that provide scores and feedback on specific error types. The system breaks down performance by exercise category and suggests a study schedule for students. The model generates its own questions based on standard reading, writing, and math formats.

stories.title: AI in the classroom
stories.summary: Inside Higher Ed surveyed 5,034 undergraduates, finding that about one-third of students use generative or agentic AI to complete coursework. While students report high satisfaction with their education, they also note that the implementation of AI tools has room for improvement.

stories.title: Engineering versus legal mindsets
stories.summary: In his book Breakneck, Dan Wang argues that China is defined by an engineering mindset while the U.S. is dominated by legal thinking. Wang suggests this framework explains why China prioritizes national development over individual rights. The book was published in August 2025.

stories.title: Akshara Gulab Ambone wins bronze at junior astronomy olympiad
stories.summary: Akshara Gulab Ambone, a student at ALLEN Career Institute, won a bronze medal at the 5th International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics for Juniors in Thailand. The event hosted 104 students from 25 countries. Hard work and guidance remain the primary drivers of international podium finishes.

stories.title: Munira Akter adds computing bronze to medal collection
stories.summary: Dhaka student Munira Akter received a 2025 International Computing Olympiad bronze medal, following a silver at the 2024 algorithms finals. The result marks her fifth international competition in five years, covering computing, algorithms, and mathematics. She continues to maintain a record of independent work in cybersecurity.

RIT students win Microsoft Hackathon
stories.summary: Five students from RIT won the Microsoft Hackathon 2026 with an AI-powered solution. The project was supported by College Mentor, a platform that connects students with mentors to provide educational insights and professional guidance.

stories.title: Abuja pupil wins UBA Foundation scholarship
stories.summary: Khaira Ojima Bala, a 15-year-old student from Abuja, won the 2026 UBA Foundation National Essay Competition. She received a 15 million naira educational grant. The competition included more than 15,000 entries from senior secondary school students across Nigeria.

stories.title: Iranian students honored for science olympiad success
Student volunteer work in San Diego
stories.summary: UC San Diego swimmer Bianca Fernandez spends Sunday mornings volunteering to distribute necessities to the unhoused community in downtown San Diego. Fernandez states that the experience provides a perspective on lives different from her own, which has become a defining part of her college career.

stories.title: BU pairs international students with mentors
stories.summary: Boston University Global Programs is pairing incoming international students with current students to help navigate campus life. The initiative aims to assist with practical challenges and cultural adjustments, from understanding grading rubrics to finding a community. Incoming students are encouraged to seek out a familiar face.

stories.title: High schoolers compete in cybersecurity and AI challenges
stories.summary: About 90 high school students participated in Mid-State Technical College’s fourth annual Tech-Con on November 13. Students from five districts engaged in hands-on challenges covering website hacking, cryptography, and artificial intelligence. The event was designed to introduce participants to potential careers in information technology.

stories.title: AI chatbot recommends Minecraft for geometry lesson
stories.summary: Researchers studying AI-powered personalized learning found that chatbots can struggle with accuracy. When asked to make a geometry lesson on circles exciting, an AI suggested a lesson on squares using Minecraft. The tool was intended to assist with personalized learning, but teacher judgment remains a requirement.

stories.title: Schools launch official Pokémon clubs
stories.summary: Educators are launching official Pokémon clubs to help students develop strategic thinking and social-emotional skills. The clubs aim to provide a low-stress environment for building community and friendships. No prior experience with the card game is required for students or coordinators to participate.

stories.title: Climate education moves beyond basic literacy
stories.summary: Educators are shifting focus toward helping young people make sense of a changing climate rather than providing more information on its existence. The approach emphasizes resilience and finding meaningful opportunities for students to participate in future planning. The goal is to help students live well with environmental changes.

stories.title: Virginia Tech publishes book on generative AI in classrooms
stories.summary: Virginia Tech Press has released Teaching History with Chatty Geeps, a book exploring how educators can use generative AI in the classroom. Authors Amy Allen and David Hicks argue for teaching with the technology rather than through it. It is the first title published by the university press.

stories.title: Virginia Tech integrates AI into liberal arts
stories.summary: Virginia Tech is incorporating artificial intelligence, data analysis, and cybersecurity into its liberal arts curriculum through the Tech for Humanity initiative. The program aims to prepare students for an AI-driven workplace while exploring the human and ethical questions behind emerging technologies.

stories.title: Georgia Tech compiles AI lessons for educators
stories.summary: Georgia Tech has released its first Academic AI Playbook, featuring 67 articles on how faculty are using the technology in classrooms. The collection compiles lessons from across seven colleges to provide practical guidance for educators. The university has been experimenting with AI in learning for several years.

stories.title: UMD professors set individual AI classroom policies
stories.summary: University of Maryland professors are establishing their own course policies regarding artificial intelligence as the technology advances. Guidelines from January 2025 require students to disclose and cite AI use on assignments. Unauthorized use is investigated by the university under existing policies for cheating and plagiarism.

stories.title: IBM and NCSC expand free cyber education for schools
stories.summary: IBM and the National Cyber Security Centre are collaborating to provide free cybersecurity and AI education to secondary schools in the UK. Materials from the CyberFirst program are now available on the IBM SkillsBuild platform. The initiative prioritizes access for disadvantaged schools and includes a new competition.

stories.title: Study habits and the science of memory
stories.summary: Research in cognitive psychology suggests that long hours of rereading and highlighting are less effective for retention than active retrieval. Learning science indicates that memory responds to the effort of recall rather than repeated exposure. Students are encouraged to use techniques that reinforce information through active processing.

stories.title: Research suggests active testing improves recall
stories.summary: A 2013 review of learning techniques found that practice testing and distributed practice are more effective than common habits like rereading or highlighting. Memory is strengthened by the effort of recall rather than repeated exposure. The findings suggest students should test themselves to improve long-term retention.

stories.title: CBSE releases physics exam questions
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has released 50 multiple-choice questions for the 2027 Class 12 Physics exam. The exam is scheduled for February 16, 2027. The board continues to emphasize competency-based questions, which remain a significant portion of the theory paper.

stories.title: CBSE provides English practice questions
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has published 50 multiple-choice questions for the 2027 Class 12 English pre-board exam. The materials cover chapters from Flamingo and Vistas. The practice set is intended to help students improve reading comprehension and analytical skills for the upcoming board examinations.

stories.title: CBSE releases biology practice questions
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has released 50 multiple-choice questions for the 2027 Class 12 Biology pre-board exam. The exam is scheduled for March 25, 2027. The questions are derived from previous years' papers to assist students with revision and conceptual understanding.

stories.title: CBSE releases math practice questions
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has compiled 50 multiple-choice questions for the 2027 Class 10 Mathematics pre-board exam. The set covers topics including algebra, geometry, and trigonometry. The practice questions are designed to help students improve calculation speed and assess preparation before final exams.

stories.title: ICSE outlines computer applications exam structure
stories.summary: The ICSE board has released the exam pattern for the 2026-27 Class 10 Computer Applications subject. The course gives equal weightage to external examinations and internal assessments. The guidelines detail the marking scheme and passing criteria for students preparing for the 2027 board examinations.

stories.title: North Penn students participate in math competition
stories.summary: North Penn students recently participated in the American Mathematics Competitions. To prepare, the school's Mu Alpha Theta cabinet organized weekly bootcamps covering topics outside the standard curriculum, such as set theory and logic. The competition challenges students to approach unfamiliar problems creatively.

stories.title: Sofia exhibition highlights Bulgarian science olympiad teams
stories.summary: A new exhibition on Sofia's Lovers' Bridge features photographs of Bulgarian students who compete in international science olympiads. The display aims to boost national pride by celebrating the participants as a new generation of awakeners. The podium is now a place for photographs as well as medals.

stories.title: Nominations open for 2027 Tri-DAC summer arts program
stories.summary: The Tri-District Arts Consortium is accepting nominations for its 41st annual summer program. Students entering grades 6 through 9 can audition for spots in creative writing, dance, and music. The program offers gifted students the opportunity to work alongside peers who share similar artistic interests.

University of Edinburgh offers full law scholarship
stories.summary: Edinburgh Law School is offering one full tuition fee waiver for an LL.M. candidate in European and Transnational Law for the 2027-2028 academic year. The scholarship is open to UK and international applicants. Competition for the single available spot closes on April 30.

stories.title: Buddy4Study foundation provides management course scholarships
stories.summary: The Buddy4Study India Foundation is offering scholarships for full-time post-graduation management courses for the 2026-27 academic year. The organization connects students with mentors to provide educational insights and content. The program aims to assist students in reaching for the stars.

stories.title: Buddy4Study foundation offers engineering scholarships
stories.summary: The Buddy4Study India Foundation has opened scholarship applications for engineering students for the 2026-27 academic year. The foundation links applicants with mentors to share experiences and educational resources. The initiative is designed to help students reach for the stars.

stories.title: National scholarship for tribal students accepting applications
stories.summary: The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is accepting applications for the 2026-27 National Scholarship for Higher Education. Eligible students receive tuition support, a ₹36,000 annual stipend, and a ₹45,000 laptop allowance. Applications for the scheme remain open until November 30.

stories.title: SC scholarship applications due November 30
stories.summary: The Central Government is accepting applications for the 2026-27 Top Class Education Scheme for SC students via the National Scholarship Portal. Eligibility is subject to income and institutional requirements. The deadline for all submissions is November 30, 2026.

stories.title: INSPIRE SHE Scholarship 2026 Application Begins, Check Steps, Eligibility and Benefits - Telegraph India
Government opens SC student scholarship portal
stories.summary: The Central Government is inviting applications for the 2026-27 Top Class Education Scheme for SC students. Eligible candidates pursuing higher education at notified institutions must submit their forms through the National Scholarship Portal by November 30. The scheme remains the primary route for official support.

stories.title: Six scholarship opportunities announced for Indian students
stories.summary: Various scholarship programs for the 2026-27 academic year are offering up to ₹75,000 and fully funded coaching for competitive exams. The support targets students in engineering, science, and professional courses. Eligibility criteria vary by financial need, gender, and disability status.

stories.title: Jay Kennedy Memorial Scholarship applications open
stories.summary: The National Cartoonists Society Foundation is accepting applications for the 2026 Jay Kennedy Memorial Scholarship. Students at 4-year colleges in the U.S., Canada, or Mexico must submit eight samples of work published in 2026. Applicants do not need to be art majors to qualify.

stories.title: 2026 Recipients Of Ferris Allen Bootstraps Scholarship Announced - Paulick Report
Rolls-Royce scholarship targets female engineering students
stories.summary: The Rolls-Royce Wings4Her Scholarship is accepting applications from female students in their first or second year of an undergraduate engineering degree. Applicants must be enrolled in AICTE-recognised institutions and maintain at least 60 percent academic merit. The deadline for online applications is November 23, 2026.

stories.title: CBSE schools ramp up exam preparation
stories.summary: With board exams approaching in 90 days, Chennai schools are increasing pre-board frequency and distributing competency-based worksheets. Zion International School has already completed one revision cycle covering half the syllabus and is moving to full-syllabus assessments. Students are currently practicing daily for physics and accountancy exams.

stories.title: CBSE sets deadline for inclusive education module
stories.summary: The Central Board of Secondary Education has directed all affiliated schools to complete the screening of its inclusive education sensitization module by 3 December 2026. This follows a previous circular from October. The board aims to build an inclusive ecosystem across its network of affiliated institutions.

stories.title: NEET PG counselling results delayed by court order
stories.summary: The Medical Counselling Committee has suspended the release of Round 2 seat allotment results following an interim order from the Madras High Court. The results, originally scheduled for today, are now on hold pending further judicial clarification. Thousands of postgraduate medical aspirants remain in a state of uncertainty.

stories.title: CISF releases exam city intimation slips
stories.summary: The Central Industrial Security Force has activated the city intimation facility for candidates registered for Constable recruitment examinations. Applicants for Fire, Tradesman, and Driver posts can now access their assigned examination locations via the official recruitment portal to facilitate travel and accommodation planning ahead of the upcoming tests.

stories.summary: Vardhman Mahaveer Open University has released the results for the Rajasthan State Certificate in Information Technology examinations held on 4 and 11 October. Candidates can access their scorecards and qualifying status through the university portal using their roll numbers or personal details without needing to visit the campus.

stories.title: JRRSU releases Shiksha Shastri admit cards
stories.summary: Jagadguru Ramanandacharya Rajasthan Sanskrit University has made admit cards available for the 2026 Shiksha Shastri examinations. Students enrolled in the first and second year of the programme, which is equivalent to a BEd, can download their hall tickets from the university website ahead of the upcoming testing period.

stories.title: Delhi schools to distribute MVPP admit cards
stories.summary: The Directorate of Education has scheduled the MVPP exam for Class 9 students on 21 November 2026. Schools are required to download and distribute admit cards between 16 and 20 November. The top 1,000 merit holders in the state-level examination will be awarded a scholarship of 5,000 rupees.

stories.title: SSB Odisha adds extra exam date for recruitment
stories.summary: The State Selection Board of Odisha has revised its recruitment schedule for Junior Assistant and Junior Clerk positions. An additional examination date has been added for 1 December 2026. The computer-based tests will now span across six days in November and December, conducted in three daily shifts.

stories.title: Maharashtra CET Cell announces 2027 exam schedule
stories.summary: The Maharashtra State Common Entrance Test Cell has released tentative dates for 2027-28 professional course admissions. Exams will run from 28 January to 10 June 2027. Many courses will now offer two attempts, with the higher percentile score being used to determine final admission eligibility for candidates.

stories.title: NCERT to release new Class 10 textbooks
stories.summary: The National Council of Educational Research and Training plans to release revised Class 10 textbooks in phases starting this November. The new curriculum materials are intended for the 2027-28 academic session. Languages including Hindi, English, Sanskrit, and Urdu are expected to be available by the end of November.

stories.title: MHT CET 2027 exam dates released
stories.summary: The State Common Entrance Test Cell of Maharashtra has published the schedule for various entrance exams, including LLB, LLM, and MBA. The first attempt for the PCB group is set for April 2027, followed by the PCM group. Second attempts for the PCB group begin in May 2027.

stories.summary: A U.S. District Judge has struck down a Trump administration rule that sought to limit international student stays to four years. stories.title: Accenture and Google Cloud launch AI education partnership
stories.summary: Accenture LearnVantage and Google Cloud have partnered to provide AI education across 1,000 schools and colleges in India. The initiative aims to establish Centres of Excellence and AI labs to promote industry-aligned learning, covering topics from generative AI to AI engineering and development for students and educators.

stories.title: Karnataka signs AI skilling agreement with five tech firms
stories.summary: The Karnataka government has signed an agreement with Google, Salesforce, Pega Systems, Sarvam AI and Gnani.ai to provide AI training. The initiative aims to skill 63,200 engineering and diploma students through specialised programmes designed to build a future-ready technology workforce in the state.

stories.title: AICTE partners with Nemetschek to upskill 150,000 students
stories.summary: The All India Council for Technical Education has partnered with the German firm Nemetschek Group to upskill 150,000 students over three years. The collaboration includes the establishment of 15 Centres of Excellence across affiliated institutions to strengthen industry-academia engagement in architecture, engineering and construction software.

stories.title: New York City Public Schools implement generative AI ban
stories.summary: New York City Public Schools is banning the use of generative artificial intelligence for students from pre-school through eighth grade for the 2026-2027 academic year. The nation's largest school district confirmed the moratorium, which restricts AI access for more than half a million students.

stories.title: College Board sues over AI cheating malware
stories.summary: The College Board is suing a developer after malware was used to feed AI-generated answers to students during the SAT. The program bypasses security features to transmit questions to a chatbot, which then displays answers on the test-taker's screen. Cheating is becoming a global exam concern.

stories.title: Cellphone bans linked to academic gains
stories.summary: Schools requiring students to lock devices in pouches saw gains equal to as much as two weeks of additional instruction per year, according to a Harvard study. The research suggests that removing phones from the classroom environment may improve overall student learning outcomes.

stories.title: University of Birmingham pauses Shakespeare Institute relocation
stories.summary: The University of Birmingham has paused plans to move its Shakespeare Institute from Stratford-upon-Avon to its city campus. Vice-chancellor Adam Tickell said the proposal is on hold while the university explores the future of the institute and its 60,000-volume library following an outcry from scholars and actors.

stories.title: Telangana to integrate classes 11 and 12 into schools
stories.summary: Telangana plans to bring Intermediate education into the school system from the 2027-28 academic year. The shift ends a 55-year arrangement where students left school after Class 10 to join separate junior colleges. The state will now adopt a 10+2 structure across three stages.

stories.title: Maharashtra nursery admission age rule changes
stories.summary: A new June 30 cut-off for nursery admissions in Maharashtra requires children to be three years old by that date. The previous cut-off was December 30. Many parents now face the prospect of their children repeating a year of playgroup to meet the revised age criteria.

stories.summary: Government schools in Himachal Pradesh currently have 4,606 vacant teaching positions. Of these, 3,256 vacancies are in general government schools, while 1,350 remain in government CBSE schools. The state has created 9,441 total government teaching posts, with 4,082 currently filled.

stories.title: Himachal Pradesh reports 4,606 vacant lecturer posts in government schools
stories.summary: The Himachal Pradesh government reported 4,606 vacant lecturer positions across its schools in a written Assembly reply. While 14,987 posts are sanctioned for general government schools, 3,256 remain unfilled. The state did not provide subject-specific breakdowns, though it noted Computer Science has the highest number of vacancies.

stories.title: Virginia opts out of federal scholarship program
stories.summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger’s office confirmed that Virginia is reversing its participation in the Education Freedom Tax Credit. The state will no longer take part in the federal scholarship program.

stories.summary: Craig Trainor has been selected to lead the Department of Justice civil rights division. During his previous tenure at the U.S. Department of Education, Trainor threatened to strip federal funding from schools over their diversity initiatives.

stories.title: Himachal Pradesh University integrates AI into curriculum
stories.summary: Himachal Pradesh University has introduced new AI courses and signed MoUs with institutions including IIT Roorkee to improve technological proficiency. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu announced a grant of Rs 5 crore for a new BTech course in AI during the university’s 77th Foundation Day celebrations.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir to mandate 25 percent private school quota
stories.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir government will soon implement a 25 percent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections and disadvantaged groups in private school entry-level seats. Education Minister Shamim Firdous said the rules for the Right to Education Act provision are in the final stage of notification.

stories.title: Indian enrolment in US master’s programs drops 34.4 percent
stories.summary: Indian enrolment in U.S. master’s programs fell 34.4 percent to 116,609 in 2025-26, according to the Open Doors report. Overall Indian student numbers in the U.S. declined 6.5 percent, with visa issuance and appointment shortages cited as primary factors behind the downturn.

stories.title: Indian medical graduates in Philippines may see licensing relief
stories.summary: Indian graduates from Philippine medical institutions may soon be eligible to take the country's Physician Licensure Examination. Ambassador Harsh Kumar Jain stated the Philippine Professional Regulation Commission has indicated that graduates can now appear for the exam and obtain registration to practise medicine.

stories.title: New Zealand expands post-study work visa eligibility
stories.summary: New Zealand has expanded its Post-Study Work Visa eligibility to include international students who complete an eligible Level 7 Graduate Diploma. Graduates can work in any occupation for up to one year. The country also introduced a six-month short-term work visa for students.

stories.title: US universities face international enrolment decline
stories.summary: New international enrolments at U.S. institutions fell 18 percent to 228,123 in 2025-26. Indian student numbers dropped 6 percent to 339,435, while Chinese numbers declined 4 percent to 254,458. Visa uncertainties and a difficult employment market are complicating the appeal of American campuses.

stories.summary: Indian student enrolment in the US fell 6.5% in 2025-26 due to a sharp decline in graduate admissions, though India remained the largest source of international students for the third consecutive year. stories.title: International student migration to OECD countries declines
stories.summary: International student migration to OECD countries fell for the second consecutive year in 2025. The decline is concentrated in Canada, the U.S., and Australia, while European countries like Germany, Italy, and Austria have registered higher inflows compared to pre-COVID levels.

stories.title: US international enrolment sees deep postgraduate losses
stories.summary: New international enrolments in the U.S. fell 18 percent in 2025-26, with significant losses in master’s programs. NAFSA projects a revenue loss of more than US$2.4 billion and 31,000 fewer jobs in 2026-27 as a result of the declining international student numbers.
